title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Risk comes from not knowing what you are doing.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

book_paragraphs: SoftTech Engineers builds the software that Indian city governments use to check and approve building plans. An architect uploads a drawing, a rule engine tests it against the local building bye-laws, and the city issues the permit and collects the fee on one system. The same company now sells digital twins to ports (its first large order is ₹92.95 crore from Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority) and runs a transferable-development-rights exchange for Mumbai. Its rule engines serve more than 1,500 cities in 18 states, FY2026 revenue was ₹132.9 crore, up 39.5%, and the business is run from Pune by its founder, Vijay Gupta [15][16][21][12].

Our new-capital verdict is REJECTED. At ₹425.90, the last TradingView print on 13 November 2026, and ₹420.95, the last verified close on 12 November, you would pay 119 times earnings for a company whose group profit after tax was ₹5.33 crore in FY2026 and whose free cash flow was negative in every year from FY2019 to FY2026 [27][37][41][42]. The business verdict is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH: real products and fast growth, but no yet-proven conversion of growth into cash.

The price, not the business, is the reason for the rejection. A reverse discounted-cash-flow model says the price needs revenue to compound at 29-35% a year for five years at a 28-32% EBITDA margin, and even management's own plan of ₹300 crore of revenue in about four years is worth ₹222 to ₹408 a share under different assumptions, all below today's price [16]. My probability-weighted FY2028E value is ₹369, which is 13.5% below the price, built from a bear value of ₹188 (30%), a base value of ₹299 (50%) and a bull value of ₹813 (20%). The pipeline's reference support band of ₹373-₹384 does not rescue the call: the base value is below it, so reward-to-risk from that band is negative. The price at which the base case alone pays 1.5 to 1 is about ₹218-₹242, 43% to 49% below the market.

Here is the debate in brief. The bull case rests on a product that is hard to remove once cities depend on it, pay-per-use revenue up 59% on the audited base (38.6% on management's own base), orders in hand of ₹302 crore, a ₹626 crore pipeline and a first half in which standalone EBITDA margin reached 32.5% [21][1]. The bear case rests on eight straight years of negative free cash flow, a credit-loss charge of ₹12.49 crore that exceeded group pre-tax profit, roughly 40% of gross trade receivables older than a year, a return on invested capital near 4%, a moat that Telangana has already breached, and a stock that trades about ₹20 lakh a day with no institutional owner [27][22][37][42]. I give the bear side more weight because its evidence is audited and the bull side's is guidance.

Across three horizons the judgments are these. Short-term trading: AVOID, because the timing gate is CAP_REJECTED, volume is balanced and the stock is too thinly traded for a tactical entry. Medium term: CONDITIONAL, pending an FY2027 audited cash-flow statement that shows positive free cash flow after capitalised development and collection days below 200. Long term: NOT PROVEN, because return on capital is about a third of the cost of capital and the evidence of repeat large orders is one port.

For your portfolio, the positions ledger shows no SoftTech shares, so the holding action is NOT_HELD and the number of shares to sell is zero. Your next marginal unit of capital goes 100% to cash. The active shortlist and the peers I screened were compared on the same-session snapshot, and none was funded, because a snapshot is not an underwriting. These are advisory alerts, not broker orders.

What would change this? Four things, any of which would send me back to rebuild the base case: audited FY2027 free cash flow after capitalised development at or above zero; days sales outstanding under 200; a credit-loss charge under ₹5 crore; or a price inside ₹218-₹242 with the base case intact. A price drop alone does not reopen the file. The evidence has to move too.

Dating and data notes. The benchmark had no verified 13 November bar, so the report is as of 12 November 2026 with the latest TradingView print noted as provisional. The market-wide Stage 2 scanner failed twice and the Q2 FY2027 call transcript (held 13 November) could not be retrieved; both are listed as gate exceptions. Chapters 1 to 6 were written price-blind and passed the blind-pass check before any price was pulled.

If I had sixty seconds with you in a lift, this is what I would say. SoftTech makes something useful that governments really use, and it is growing. It has never yet turned that growth into spare cash for its shareholders, and the market is asking you to pay for the day it does. At this price, I would rather wait for the evidence than pay for the promise.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A good business and a good investment are two different questions. Chapters 1 to 6 asked the first one without looking at the price, and the answer was promising but unproven. Chapters 7 to 9 asked the second one, and the answer was no at this price. Keeping the two apart is how you avoid falling in love with the story.
